Apple___Apple_scab.description: A fungal disease that causes dark olive to brown lesions on apple leaves and fruit.
symptoms: Dark spots on leaves
Leaf distortion
Premature leaf drop
Scabby lesions on fruit
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Remove and destroy infected fallen leaves and affected plant material. Use an appropriate fungicide according to the product label and local agricultural guidance.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Maintain good orchard sanitation, prune for better air circulation, and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

Apple___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease that can affect apple leaves, branches, and fruit.
symptoms: Frogeye-like leaf spots, dead branches, and dark rotting lesions on fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Remove infected fruit, dead wood, and diseased plant material. Apply an appropriate fungicide according to local recommendations and the product label.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Remove mummified fruit and dead branches, maintain orchard sanitation, and avoid plant injuries.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: A fungal disease that causes characteristic yellow-orange lesions on apple leaves.
symptoms: Yellow-orange spots on leaves that may develop dark centers and produce thread-like structures.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Remove nearby alternate hosts where practical and use an appropriate fungicide according to local agricultural recommendations.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Maintain good orchard sanitation and reduce proximity to susceptible cedar and juniper hosts where feasible.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease that causes spots on tomato leaves, stems, and fruit.
symptoms: Small dark leaf spots, yellow halos, and raised lesions on fruit.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Remove infected material and use approved bacterial disease-management products according to local agricultural recommendations.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use disease-free seed, avoid overhead irrigation, rotate crops, and maintain sanitation.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease that commonly affects older tomato leaves first.
symptoms: Dark spots with concentric rings, yellowing leaves, and progressive defoliation.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Remove infected leaves and debris and use an appropriate fungicide according to local recommendations.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops, mulch soil to reduce splash, maintain airflow, and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: A rapidly developing disease that can severely damage tomato foliage and fruit.
symptoms: Dark water-soaked lesions, rapid browning, and possible white fungal growth under humid conditions.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Remove infected material and use an appropriate late-blight management program according to local recommendations.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Use resistant varieties where available, improve airflow, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, and scout frequently.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: A fungal disease favored by high humidity and poor air circulation.
symptoms: Yellow patches on the upper leaf surface with olive-green to brown growth underneath.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Remove infected leaves and improve ventilation. Use an appropriate fungicide according to local recommendations when necessary.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Reduce humidity, improve airflow, avoid wetting foliage, and maintain adequate plant spacing.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: A fungal disease that causes numerous small spots on tomato leaves.
symptoms: Small circular spots with dark margins and pale centers, often beginning on lower leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Remove infected leaves and plant debris and use an appropriate fungicide according to local recommendations.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Use mulch, avoid overhead irrigation, improve airflow, and rotate crops.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: A pest infestation that can cause stippling and decline of tomato foliage.
symptoms: Fine yellow stippling, bronzing, leaf drying, and sometimes visible webbing.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Use appropriate integrated pest management measures and an approved miticide only when necessary and according to the label.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Monitor leaf undersides regularly, reduce plant stress, conserve beneficial insects, and avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum insecticides.

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: A fungal disease that produces brown lesions with concentric rings on tomato foliage and fruit.
symptoms: Circular brown lesions with target-like rings and possible fruit spotting.
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment: Remove infected material and use an appropriate fungicide according to local recommendations.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Improve airflow, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, use clean planting material, and maintain sanitation.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: A viral disease commonly transmitted by whiteflies.
symptoms: Leaf curling, yellowing, stunted growth, and reduced fruit production.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: There is no direct cure for infected plants. Remove severely infected plants where appropriate and manage the whitefly vector.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Use resistant varieties, disease-free transplants, insect exclusion or monitoring, and effective whitefly management.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: A viral disease that can cause mottled foliage and reduced plant growth.
symptoms: Mosaic light and dark green patterns, leaf distortion, and reduced plant vigor.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: There is no curative treatment for infected plants. Remove affected plants and sanitize tools and hands.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use certified seed, control weeds, sanitize tools, and avoid spreading sap between plants.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: A complex grapevine disease associated with fungal pathogens that can affect leaves, shoots, and fruit.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: Remove severely affected plant material and manage infected vines according to local viticulture guidance.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Use clean planting material, protect pruning wounds, and maintain vineyard sanitation.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Improve canopy ventilation, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, and maintain vineyard sanitation.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: A serious citrus disease associated with bacteria and transmitted by psyllid insects.
symptoms: Blotchy leaf mottling, yellow shoots, poor fruit development, and premature fruit drop.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment: There is no simple curative treatment for infected trees. Follow local citrus disease management guidance and manage the insect vector.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Use certified disease-free planting material, monitor and manage psyllid vectors, and remove infected trees where required by local programs.
